title: Late Breaking Results: BLAST: Bisection-Free Learning Approach for Statistical Timing Characterization
problem: Statistical timing characterization of standard cells requires laborious bisection analysis to extract setup/hold constraints for sequential cells, creating computational bottlenecks in timing closure workflows.
motivation: Timing characterization is critical path in design sign-off, but iterative bisection searches for constraint refinement consume significant compute resources and wall-clock time, limiting design iteration speed.
method: BLAST extracts inherent delay for data and clock paths in sequential cells as features, then applies multi-task learning with a multi-gate mixture-of-experts (MMoE) model to exploit interdependencies between setup and hold constraints. Active learning strategy improves training efficiency by focusing on high-value samples.
key_novelty: First bisection-free statistical timing characterization using multi-task MMoE learning to predict setup/hold constraints directly from path delays, achieving 76.9% runtime reduction.
contributions: Feature extraction of inherent path delays (data and clock) for timing constraint prediction.
Multi-task MMoE model exploiting setup-hold constraint interdependencies.
Active learning strategy achieving 76.9% runtime reduction vs commercial tools with 2.21% rRMSE and 0.82ps WCAE.
primary_theme: bisection-free statistical timing via multi-task learning
